The practical guidance (archive model hash + sampler + steps + CFG + resolution + scheduler + workflow JSON + seed; embed the ComfyUI workflow in the PNG; treat the workflow file as source of truth with the seed as one field; do not expect bit-identical output across machines or library upgrades) is fully consistent with the source. CONFIRMED.
- **Sources:** [About Reproducibility (Discussion #7809)](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui/discussions/7809) (AUTOMATIC1111 stable-diffusion-webui contributors, 2023) — Exact reproduction needs matching seed, sampler, steps, CFG, resolution, WebUI/PyTorch versions, GPU architecture, and disabled non-deterministic optimizations (xformers); different GPU architectures deviate substantially.

### A fixed seed does NOT deliver character consistency across… · `recommended` · community-claim

**A fixed seed does NOT deliver character consistency across images. Consistency comes from prompt identity-blocks, reference conditioning (IP-Adapter/ControlNet), or a trained LoRA — NOT from reusing the seed.**

Holding the seed fixed only holds the STARTING noise fixed; the moment you change the prompt (new scene, new pose) the denoising trajectory diverges and the character changes. Same-seed-same-prompt = same image is a tautology, not consistency across DIFFERENT images. Empirically the reliable consistency methods are: (1) a fixed verbatim character description block in every prompt, (2) reference/pose conditioning to separate identity from scene, and (3) a LoRA fine-tuned on 10-20 images of the character (cited at ~85-95% feature retention). The 'lock the seed for a consistent character' tip is folklore — it is the weakest lever of the four.  [grounding: strong-community]

- **For the pipeline:** For a recurring JRPG character across many shots, do NOT rely on a fixed seed for identity. Build identity from: a frozen character token-block pasted verbatim into every prompt + IP-Adapter/reference image for the face + a trained character LoRA for production volume. Vary the seed freely between shots to get pose/expression variety — identity is held by the LoRA/reference, not the integer. If two shots of the same character look different, fix the reference/LoRA/prompt-block, not the seed.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** all · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CONFIRMED: Confirmed against the cited community source thinkpeak.ai, which states a fixed seed for consistency is 'brittle' -- 'A fixed seed with a changed prompt often results in a completely different composition' -- and that reliable identity comes from a repeated character-description block (its 'Three-Point' system), reference conditioning (it calls IP-Adapter FaceID the 'superior solution'), and LoRA fine-tuning; identity drift is solved by 'engineering discipline, not random luck.' The second citation (Medium/Bootcamp 2025) timed out and could not be fetched, but it is corroborative-only; the primary source fully supports the claim. This is also the mechanistically correct position: the seed only sets the starting noise; cross-image identity is a CONDITIONING property (prompt tokens + reference adapters + trained weights), not a property of the initial noise draw. Strong CONFIRMED -- a 'fixed seed = same character' belief is genuine folklore and the sources debunk it.
- **Sources:** [How to Keep Characters Consistent Across AI Scenes / SD Character Consistency 2026](https://thinkpeak.ai/stable-diffusion-character-consistency-tutorial/) (skywork.ai / thinkpeak.ai, 2026) — Seed alone is insufficient for character consistency; reliable methods are a fixed character description block, ControlNet/reference conditioning, and LoRA fine-tuning. ; [How to Design Consistent AI Characters with Prompts, Diffusion & Reference Control](https://medium.com/design-bootcamp/how-to-design-consistent-ai-characters-with-prompts-diffusion-reference-control-2025-a1bf1757655d) (Shweta Kaushal (Bootcamp/Medium), 2025) — Character identity is held by reference control and trained adapters/LoRA, not by reusing the random seed.

### there is no UNIVERSAL magic/lucky seed. 'Golden' seeds… · `recommended` · reproduced-from-source

**FOLKLORE ZONE: there is no UNIVERSAL magic/lucky seed. 'Golden' seeds measurably exist but the quality gap is modest and the ranking is model-specific — seed quality is conditional, not magic.**

The one empirical study on this (Xu et al., 'Good Seed Makes a Good Crop', arXiv:2405.14828) found the best 'golden' seed scored FID 21.60 vs the worst 'inferior' seed 31.97 on SD 2.0 — a real but bounded ~48% gap, and the seed rankings were derived PER MODEL (separate golden seeds for SD 2.0 vs SDXL Turbo). The paper itself admits the mechanism is opaque ('it is unclear what makes seeds easily discernible'). So a seed can bias toward better average composition/quality for a given model+prompt-set, but no seed is a portable cheat code that makes any prompt good. The community 'this seed always gives great faces' claim is folklore: it survives only within one fixed model+prompt+resolution+sampler configuration.  [grounding: empirical-paper]

- **For the pipeline:** Do NOT maintain a personal 'lucky seed' list and expect it to improve unrelated prompts. Treat seeds as interchangeable lottery tickets within a config. If you want a quality edge, do a quick seed-sweep (e.g. 8-16 seeds) for a SPECIFIC frozen prompt+model and pick the winner FOR THAT shot only — never carry it forward as a universal asset. Quality lives in the prompt, model, and CFG, not in a blessed integer.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** all · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CORRECTED: Core claim CONFIRMED with one factual correction. The cited paper 'Good Seed Makes a Good Crop' (Xu/Li et al. 2024, arxiv 2405.14828v1) confirms: (a) golden seeds measurably exist (golden seed 469 on SD 2.0 reached FID 21.60 vs inferior seed 696 at FID 31.97); (b) they were identified SEPARATELY per model (k=65 golden seeds for SD 2.0, k=67 for SDXL Turbo) -- model-specific, not universal; (c) the authors EXPLICITLY admit the mechanism is unclear ('it remains unclear what makes seeds easily discernible'). CORRECTION: the gap is NOT 'modest.' The paper characterizes the 10.37-point FID difference as 'significant within the community' -- substantial, not modest. SECOND NUANCE that strengthens the user's safe-practice rule but complicates the wording: the paper finds seed RANKINGS are 'generalizable across a different set of prompts' WITHIN a fixed model -- so within one model+config a golden seed does carry some edge across prompts, which is more than 'interchangeable lottery tickets.' The correct framing: no UNIVERSAL (cross-model) magic seed, mechanism unknown, gaps real and significant; a quick seed-sweep for a frozen prompt+model is the right way to capture the edge, and a per-model (not global) seed note is defensible. The blanket 'treat seeds as interchangeable lottery tickets' overstates the debunk -- within a single model, ranked seeds are reproducibly better.
- **Sources:** [Good Seed Makes a Good Crop: Discovering Secret Seeds in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.14828v1) (Xu, Li, et al., 2024) — Best golden seed FID 21.60 vs worst 31.97; golden seeds identified separately per model (SD 2.0, SDXL Turbo); mechanism admitted unclear. arXiv:2405.14828

### A good seed does NOT survive a resolution change. Changing… · `recommended` · community-claim

**A good seed does NOT survive a resolution change. Changing width or height — even by a few pixels — reshapes the noise tensor, so the same seed yields a different noise pattern and a different image.**

Resolution is the SHAPE of the latent noise tensor (e.g. 4x64x64 for 512x512, 4x96x64 for a portrait). The seed fills that tensor element-by-element; change the tensor dimensions and the RNG fills a differently-shaped array, producing fundamentally different noise. There is no meaningful correspondence between 'seed 469 at 1024x1024' and 'seed 469 at 832x1216'. Tools' 'seed resize' features only approximate visual similarity and explicitly fail with ancestral samplers.  [grounding: strong-community]

- **For the pipeline:** Lock your generation resolution BEFORE seed-sweeping for a character shot. Never sweep at low res then bump resolution expecting the same composition — re-sweep at the final resolution, or generate at the locked res and upscale via img2img / Hires-fix / a dedicated upscaler (which preserves the image, not the seed). For a portrait pipeline, pick one canonical aspect ratio per shot type and freeze it.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** all · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CONFIRMED: Mechanism confirmed, though NOT from the exact getimg.ai URL cited (that page only covers basic seed concepts and does not mention tensor shape or resolution). The OTHER cited source -- stable-diffusion-art's 'How Stable Diffusion works' -- does support it: the latent image tensor is 4x64x64 for 512x512 and 4x96x64 for a 768x512 image, the seed sets the random latent tensor, and resolution is encoded in that tensor's shape. Therefore changing width/height changes the tensor shape, so the same seed fills a differently-shaped tensor and produces a different noise pattern and image. Independent corroboration: the AUTOMATIC1111 webui ships a dedicated 'seed resize' feature precisely because seeds do NOT naturally survive a resolution change. The practice (lock res before sweeping; upscale via img2img/Hires-fix/upscaler which preserves the image not the seed) is sound. Minor sourcing note: cite the stable-diffusion-art article, not getimg.ai, for the tensor-shape detail.
- **Sources:** [Guide to using Seed in Stable Diffusion / How Stable Diffusion works](https://getimg.ai/guides/guide-to-seed-parameter-in-stable-diffusion) (getimg.ai / stable-diffusion-art, 2024) — Latent tensor shape encodes resolution (4x64x64 vs 4x96x64); changing resolution applies the seed to a different-shaped tensor, giving a completely different noise pattern and image.

### A good seed does NOT transfer across different models or… · `recommended` · reproduced-from-source

**A good seed does NOT transfer across different models or samplers. The same integer produces a totally different (and not-necessarily-good) image on a different checkpoint or sampler.**

The seed only selects a point in the noise distribution; it carries no meaning by itself. A different model has different learned weights and a different denoising function, so the same starting noise lands somewhere completely different. A different sampler walks a different ODE/SDE trajectory from the same start. The empirical paper found golden seeds had to be re-discovered per architecture (SD 2.0 vs SDXL Turbo). For a studio running SDXL, Chroma/FLUX, Qwen-Image, and Z-Image side by side, a seed tuned on SDXL is meaningless on FLUX.  [grounding: empirical-paper]

- **For the pipeline:** When you switch checkpoint (SDXL -> FLUX/Chroma/Qwen/Z-Image) or sampler, DISCARD the seed — do not copy it expecting the same look. Re-sweep seeds fresh on the new model. Keep a per-model seed note, never a global one. If a shot looked great on SDXL and you must port it to FLUX, port the PROMPT and reference image, not the seed.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** all · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CONFIRMED: Cross-MODEL non-transfer is confirmed: 'Good Seed Makes a Good Crop' (Xu/Li et al. 2024, arxiv 2405.14828v1) discovered golden seeds separately for SD 2.0 and SDXL Turbo, with different golden-seed sets per model -- seed quality does not transfer across architectures, and a raw seed integer feeding a different checkpoint's noise sampler yields an unrelated initial latent. Cross-SAMPLER non-transfer is also true but the SPECIFIC secondary citation is weak: the AUTOMATIC1111 'Seed-breaking-changes' wiki does NOT actually state that ancestral samplers fail to preserve seed-conditioned results across configurations (it documents a list of noise-schedule / parsing / sampler-timing changes that break reproducibility between webui versions). The sampler-stability point is properly supported by finding 6's sources, not this wiki page. Net verdict CONFIRMED because the load-bearing transfer claim holds and the practice (re-sweep on a new model/sampler, keep per-model notes, port prompt+reference not seed) is correct; one supporting citation is mis-attributed but a valid source for the claim exists elsewhere in the set.
- **Sources:** [Good Seed Makes a Good Crop: Discovering Secret Seeds in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.14828v1) (Xu, Li, et al., 2024) — Golden seeds were discovered separately for SD 2.0 and SDXL Turbo, indicating seed quality is model-specific and non-transferable across architectures. arXiv:2405.14828 ; [Seed breaking changes (Wiki) + Samplers guide](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui/wiki/Seed-breaking-changes) (AUTOMATIC1111 / stable-diffusion-art, 2023) — Different samplers handle the seed differently; ancestral samplers in particular do not preserve seed-conditioned results across configurations.

### The seed only sets the START of the denoising trajectory… · `recommended` · reproduced-from-source

**The seed only sets the START of the denoising trajectory (the initial noise latent); the PROMPT + CFG decide WHAT subject/identity/composition the trajectory converges toward. A generic-nobody character is a prompt miss, not a seed miss.**

In latent diffusion (Rombach 2022) the seed seeds the RNG that fills the initial Gaussian noise tensor — it picks one starting point in latent space. The reverse/denoising process (DDPM, Ho 2020) is then STEERED at every step by text conditioning injected through cross-attention, amplified by classifier-free guidance (Ho & Salimans 2022): the final score = unconditional + CFG*(conditional - unconditional). So the seed answers 'which of many valid images for THIS prompt', while the prompt+CFG answer 'what is in the image at all'. If the subject is wrong/generic/slouching, re-rolling the seed just samples a different generic-nobody from the same wrong prompt distribution. The operator's wasted re-render + tonemap tweaks were treating a conditioning failure as a sampling failure.  [grounding: official-docs]

- **For the pipeline:** DECISION RULE on a bad result: if the image is COMPETENT but you wanted a different pose/crop/variation of the SAME correct subject -> re-roll the seed. If the SUBJECT, identity, body language, or composition is wrong (generic nobody, wrong silhouette, missing the character's defining traits) -> STOP re-rolling, rewrite the prompt and/or raise CFG. Seed re-rolls cannot fix a conditioning miss. Add the character's load-bearing identity tokens (silhouette, posture, signature features) and confirm CFG is in the 4-8 adherence band before touching the seed.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** all · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CONFIRMED: Verified against the cited primary sources. DDPM (Ho/Jain/Abbeel 2020, arxiv 2006.11239) full text confirms the reverse process starts from initial Gaussian noise p(x_T)=N(x_T;0,I) and proceeds as a LEARNED Markov chain p_theta(x_{t-1}|x_t) -- i.e. the seed fixes the trajectory's starting point, the learned model (conditioned on the prompt) drives where it goes. Classifier-Free Guidance (Ho/Salimans 2022, arxiv 2207.12598) confirms higher guidance scale increases adherence to the conditioning (prompt) at the cost of diversity. LDM (Rombach et al. 2022, arxiv 2112.10752) confirms text conditioning enters the UNet via cross-attention layers, steering denoising independently of the noise seed. The decision rule is a sound engineering corollary of this mechanism: re-rolling the seed only repositions the start of the trajectory under the SAME conditioning, so it cannot repair a conditioning (subject/identity) miss -- only a different draw of the same competent subject. No correction needed.
- **Sources:** [Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239) (Ho, Jain, Abbeel, 2020) — Defines the reverse denoising process from an initial Gaussian noise sample; the noise sets the trajectory start, the learned model drives where it goes. arXiv:2006.11239 ; [Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.12598) (Ho, Salimans, 2022) — Higher guidance scale makes the model follow the conditioning (prompt) more strongly; the prompt, amplified by CFG, governs subject adherence, not the seed. arXiv:2207.12598

### CFG controls HOW HARD the prompt steers the trajectory away… · `recommended` · reproduced-from-source

**CFG controls HOW HARD the prompt steers the trajectory away from the unconditional (seed-only) direction -- it is the prompt's volume knob, not a content knob.**

CFG = eps_uncond + w*(eps_cond - eps_uncond). At w=1 the prompt barely steers (you drift toward the seed's generic unconditional reconstruction -> bland). Raising w pushes harder toward the prompt manifold (more literal adherence) but too-high w over-saturates, fries detail, and collapses diversity. Low CFG = creativity/seed dominates; high CFG = prompt dominates literally. Crucially, CFG cannot inject information the prompt never stated -- it can only amplify the steering force of whatever IS in the prompt.  [grounding: empirical-paper]

- **For the pipeline:** If the model is IGNORING a good detailed prompt (you described the scar, it has no scar), nudge CFG up before re-rolling. If results look fried/over-contrasted/plasticky, lower CFG. But if the prompt is vague, raising CFG just makes a generic image more aggressively generic -- fix the prompt first, CFG second, seed third.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** all · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CONFIRMED: Classifier-Free Guidance (Ho & Salimans 2022, arxiv 2207.12598) abstract confirms guidance combines conditional and unconditional estimates to trade off sample quality against diversity. The DeepWiki source confirms the directional mechanism: w=0 ignores the prompt (uncond only), w>1 gives stronger prompt adherence via extrapolation. The 'volume knob not content knob' framing is correct -- CFG amplifies adherence to whatever the prompt already says; it cannot inject detail the prompt omitted. The ordering rule (prompt first, CFG second, seed third) follows directly: raising CFG on a vague prompt only makes a generic image more aggressively generic. Confirmed.
- **Sources:** [Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.12598) (Ho, Salimans, 2022) — Guidance interpolates/extrapolates between conditional and unconditional noise predictions; the scale w trades off sample fidelity to the conditioning against diversity and quality. arXiv:2207.12598 ; [Guidance Scale and Prompt Adherence](https://deepwiki.com/stephencwelch/ai_book/10.4-guidance-scale-and-prompt-adherence) (DeepWiki (ai_book), 2024) — Low CFG -> model creativity dominates (more abstract/unexpected); high CFG -> prompt direction dominates (faithful/literal); high CFG improves adherence but degrades quality.

### Correct CFG range is model-family-specific · `recommended` · community-claim

**Correct CFG range is model-family-specific; using SDXL-era CFG on a distilled/flow model (FLUX/Chroma) is itself a cause of 'bad' results that gets misread as a seed problem.**

SD1.5/SDXL want real CFG ~6-8 to follow CLIP prompts. FLUX-dev is guidance-distilled and uses a low distilled 'guidance' value (~1-1.5 typical, sometimes called CFG=1 in samplers); pushing real CFG high on it burns the image. Chroma (FLUX-schnell-derived) and Qwen-Image / Z-Image (MMDiT + large text encoders) have their own defaults. A character that looks washed-out or over-cooked may be a CFG/family mismatch, not a seed or prompt failure.  [grounding: strong-community]

- **For the pipeline:** Lock the family-correct guidance FIRST so prompt adherence is honest: SDXL ~6-8, FLUX-dev distilled-guidance ~1-1.5 (real CFG 1), Chroma/Qwen per their model card. Only once guidance is correct can you trust the 'is this a prompt miss or seed miss' diagnosis -- otherwise a guidance bug masquerades as both.
- **Engine:** T5 · **Base:** FLUX · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CONFIRMED: Studio Angry Shark (Medium) confirms exact ranges verbatim: Flux 1.0-1.5, SD1.5/SDXL 6.0-8.0, and that mismatched CFG breaks output (Flux at 7.0+ 'completely breaks generation, destroys quality'; SD at 1.0 'ignores your prompt'). DeepWiki corroborates the underlying adherence/quality tradeoff. The claim that a guidance-family bug masquerades as both a prompt miss AND a seed miss is well-reasoned and the 'lock guidance first so the diagnosis is honest' sequencing is correct. One clarification on terminology in the prompt_rule: FLUX-dev uses a 'distilled guidance' embedding at ~3.5 (model-native) while the sampler's true CFG is held at 1.0 -- so 'FLUX-dev ~1-1.5 (real CFG 1)' is roughly right but conflates the two knobs; the practical instruction to follow the model card per family is the safe rule and is correct.
- **Sources:** [ComfyUI Generation Parameters / Common Mistakes](https://medium.com/@studio.angry.shark/5-critical-comfyui-mistakes-that-frustrate-beginners-and-how-to-fix-them-81e833d4eb58) (Studio Angry Shark (Medium), 2024) — Different model families need different CFG: Flux ~1.0-1.5, SD1.5/SDXL ~6.0-8.0 to follow prompts properly; wrong CFG for the family produces poor output. ; [The Most Complete Guide to Stable Diffusion Parameters](https://openart.ai/blog/post/the-most-complete-guide-to-stable-diffusion-parameters) (OpenArt, 2024) — CFG controls prompt adherence vs creativity; appropriate ranges differ by model and too-high CFG degrades image quality.

### Same seed + edited prompt = global structure preserved with… · `recommended` · community-claim

**Same seed + edited prompt = global structure preserved with changed content, which is the controlled way to A/B test a prompt edit.**

Holding the seed fixed and changing only the prompt keeps the broad layout/pose/color basin roughly stable while swapping the semantic content (e.g., change one emotion word -> expression changes, hair/clothes/background largely persist). This is because the trajectory starts from the same z_T and only the conditioning vector differs, so early structure is shared before the prompt pulls content apart. This isolates the variable: you SEE what your word change actually did.  [grounding: strong-community]

- **For the pipeline:** When tuning prompt wording, FREEZE the seed (and use a deterministic sampler) and change one phrase at a time -- this turns 'did my edit help?' from guesswork into a clean before/after. Once the wording is right, THEN unfreeze the seed and batch-roll to pick the best instance. Freeze-seed for prompt science; roll-seed for instance selection.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** all · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CORRECTED: The CORE claim is confirmed: promptingpixels and the Medium 'same face' article both confirm same-seed + edited-prompt retains structural similarities while content changes, and the 'freeze seed + deterministic sampler + change one phrase at a time' A/B methodology is correct and genuinely useful. CORRECTION on the over-claim hiding in the supporting evidence: the cited sources do NOT support reliable IDENTITY/face consistency via a fixed seed. promptingpixels explicitly warns this 'isn't a reliable way to make consistent images of different subjects.' The Medium article only demonstrates 'similar-but-different' images and does NOT validate that facial bone structure/identity stays fixed across prompt edits -- it shows resemblance, not a locked identity. So: use freeze-seed for clean prompt A/B (valid), but do NOT rely on a frozen seed as a character-identity lock across different prompts or different characters (that is the seed-consistency folklore, and it fails). For true cross-image identity, the field uses IP-Adapter / reference-conditioning / LoRA / InstantID, not a shared seed. The prompt_rule as written is fine; just don't let 'global structure preserved' drift into 'same character guaranteed.'
- **Sources:** [How to Create the Same Face in Different Images](https://medium.com/@javier.rebollo_35487/how-to-create-the-same-face-in-different-images-f865ca4ed327) (Javier Inspiralia (Medium), 2023) — Keeping the same seed and changing the prompt slightly (e.g., one emotion word) changes the targeted attribute while preserving other features like hair, clothes, and background. ; [What is a Seed When Working With Stable Diffusion Models?](https://www.promptingpixels.com/tutorial/seed-value) (Prompting Pixels, 2024) — Same seed with a changed prompt yields a changed image that retains structural similarities; the seed fixes the noise start while the prompt steers content.

### The sampler determines the PATH from the seed's noise to… · `recommended` · community-claim

**The sampler determines the PATH from the seed's noise to the image; ancestral (stochastic) samplers inject fresh noise each step, so they partly override the seed's determinism.**

Given a fixed seed (z_T) and prompt, the sampler chooses the integration path of the reverse ODE/SDE. Deterministic samplers (DDIM, Euler, DPM++ 2M) follow a fixed path -> same seed reproduces exactly and converges as steps increase. Ancestral/SDE samplers (Euler a, DPM++ SDE) add NEW random noise at every step, so the same seed + same prompt can yield different images at different step counts and never fully 'settle.' This means with Euler a, some apparent variation is sampler stochasticity, not the seed.  [grounding: strong-community]

- **For the pipeline:** For reproducible character iteration where you want the SEED to be the only variable, use a deterministic sampler (DDIM / Euler / DPM++ 2M). Reserve ancestral samplers (Euler a) for when you WANT extra variety. If you are A/B testing prompt edits, a deterministic sampler isolates the prompt's effect cleanly; an ancestral one muddies it.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** sampler-specific · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CONFIRMED: RunDiffusion source confirms Euler-ancestral 'introduces a certain degree of random noise' at each iteration and 'if the process were to be repeated, the outcome would differ,' contrasting with deterministic samplers that reproduce with identical seed/params. (The stable-diffusion-art.com URL returned HTTP 403 and could not be fetched, but the second cited source fully corroborates.) Precision note on 'partly override the seed's determinism': in most implementations the per-step ancestral noise is itself derived from the same seeded RNG, so a fixed seed + fixed step count + fixed sampler IS reproducible -- the non-determinism shows up as sensitivity to step count and as failure to converge, exactly as the source says. So the practical guidance (use DDIM/Euler/DPM++ 2M to isolate the prompt's effect in A/B tests; reserve Euler a for variety) is correct, even if 'override the seed' slightly overstates the mechanism.
- **Sources:** [Stable Diffusion Samplers: A Comprehensive Guide](https://stable-diffusion-art.com/samplers/) (Andrew / Stable Diffusion Art, 2024) — Ancestral samplers add random noise at each step so images do not converge and vary with step count; DDIM/Euler are deterministic and reproduce consistently. ; [Sampling Methods in Stable Diffusion](https://learn.rundiffusion.com/sampling-methods/) (RunDiffusion, 2024) — Euler-ancestral denoising depends on unique random noise injected at each iteration, producing different results even with the same seed/prompt across step counts.

### The seed only chooses the starting Gaussian noise latent · `recommended` · reproduced-from-source

**The seed only chooses the starting Gaussian noise latent; it carries no semantic content of its own.**

Generation begins from a pure-noise latent z_T sampled deterministically from the seed. The denoising network then walks z_T -> z_0 conditioned on the prompt (DDPM reverse process, Ho 2020; latent-space version Rombach 2022). The seed is just the random-number-generator state that fixes z_T byte-for-byte. It does NOT encode 'a slouching man' or any concept -- it is a fixed cloud of static that the model interprets THROUGH the prompt. Same seed + same prompt + same sampler/steps/CFG = pixel-identical image (full determinism); change any one and the trajectory diverges.  [grounding: empirical-paper]

- **For the pipeline:** Treat the seed as a coordinate, not a content knob. If the IMAGE CONTENT is wrong (generic character, wrong attributes, wrong vibe), the seed is not the lever -- rewrite the prompt. Only re-roll the seed when the content is right but you want a different SAMPLE (different pose/face/framing) of that same described thing.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** all · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CONFIRMED: Verified against both cited papers. DDPM (Ho et al. 2020, arxiv 2006.11239) defines the reverse process as starting from Gaussian noise x_T ~ N(0,I) with the model predicting noise to remove at each step. LDM (Rombach et al. 2022, arxiv 2112.10752) abstract confirms denoising in latent space with text/conditioning entering via cross-attention layers. The architectural claim is textbook-correct: the noise sample is the random starting point and the prompt drives content. The prompt_rule (seed = coordinate not content knob; re-roll only for a different sample of an already-correct description) is the right operational consequence. Caveat worth knowing: the seed is not 100% semantically inert in practice -- finding #6 shows seeds carry distinct structural signatures and bias composition -- but it carries no PROMPT-LEVEL semantic content (it cannot make a character wear armor you never described), which is the load-bearing point here.
- **Sources:** [Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239) (Ho, Jain, Abbeel, 2020) — Defines the reverse denoising process starting from Gaussian noise x_T ~ N(0,I); the noise sample is the random starting point, the model predicts the noise to remove at each step. arXiv:2006.11239 ; [High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.10752) (Rombach, Blattmann, Lorenz, Esser, Ommer, 2022) — Denoising runs in latent space from a noisy latent z_T; text condition c enters via cross-attention (CLIP embeddings as keys/values), so prompt drives content while z_T is the noise start. arXiv:2112.10752

### The seed primarily fixes COMPOSITION, POSE, FRAMING, and… · `recommended` · community-claim

**The seed primarily fixes COMPOSITION, POSE, FRAMING, and the specific face/identity instance; the prompt fixes WHAT content, attributes, and style are allowed.**

Because the initial noise determines where the model finds 'hooks' to grow structure, the seed strongly correlates with object arrangement, camera angle, body pose, and which specific face/instance is sampled. The prompt is the semantic constraint set: it says 'armored knight, scar, determined expression' but does not by itself pick which of infinitely many valid knights you get. Empirically, low-level traits (color palette, object pose, layout) persist across prompts when the noise is held fixed, while the prompt governs identity of content and style.  [grounding: strong-community]

- **For the pipeline:** Diagnose by category. POSE / FRAMING / LAYOUT / which-face-you-got = SEED territory (re-roll). WHAT the character IS (clothing, age, expression descriptors, art style, mood) = PROMPT territory (rewrite). A 'generic slouching nobody' is two things: 'slouching' is partly seed (pose), but 'nobody / generic' is a PROMPT miss -- you never told it who this person is.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** all · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CONFIRMED: arxiv 2411.18810 abstract confirms 'different initial random seeds tend to guide the model to place objects in distinct image areas, potentially adhering to specific patterns of camera angles and image composition associated with the seed' -- direct support for seed = composition/camera/layout. The getimg.ai source supports prompt = content. The diagnostic framing (pose/framing/which-face = seed territory; what-the-character-IS = prompt territory; 'generic nobody' is a prompt miss) is correct and actionable. Minor precision note: 'the specific face/identity instance' is seed-influenced but NOT seed-LOCKED -- see finding #7; a seed biases the face you get but does not reliably pin a stable identity across prompt edits. The category-diagnosis rule itself stands.

### Seeds DO vary in quality, but that quality is largely… · `recommended` · reproduced-from-source

**Seeds DO vary in quality, but that quality is largely PROMPT-SPECIFIC, not a portable 'magic number' -- the magic-seed folklore is partly real, mostly false.**

Empirically, seeds are not equal: across 1,024 seeds, a 'golden' seed reached FID 21.60 vs an 'inferior' seed's 31.97 (Good Seed Makes a Good Crop); compositional accuracy swung 41.0% vs 28.3% across seeds for multi-object prompts (All Seeds Are Not Equal). A classifier can ID the generating seed with >99.9% accuracy -- seeds leave a structural fingerprint. BUT: there is no correlation between the seed NUMBER and the output, and a seed's goodness does not reliably transfer to a different subject/prompt. So 'seed 12345 is lucky for everything' is FOLKLORE; 'for THIS prompt, some noise samples place the figure better than others' is real.  [grounding: empirical-paper]

- **For the pipeline:** Do not hoard 'magic seeds' as portable assets across characters -- a good seed for one prompt is not good for another. The legit move: once your PROMPT is dialed, batch 4-8 seeds and curate the best composition/pose; pin that seed for THAT exact prompt for reproducibility. Never use a fixed favorite seed as a substitute for writing a strong prompt.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** all · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CONFIRMED: The empirical core is verified hard: 'Good Seed Makes a Good Crop' (arxiv 2405.14828) abstract confirms golden seed FID 21.60 vs inferior 31.97 across 1024 SD2.0 seeds, and a classifier predicting the seed from the image with >99.9% accuracy -- so seeds genuinely leave distinct structural signatures and DO vary in quality. The anti-folklore framing is the right verdict and survives a hard look: there is NO evidence for a portable universal magic seed, and the 'pin a seed per dialed prompt, don't hoard across characters' rule is exactly the disciplined move. Two caveats on the specifics: (a) the cited '41.0% down to 28.3%' compositional-accuracy figure for 2411.18810 was NOT in that paper's abstract (it reports relative increases like 60.7% spatial, 29.3% numerical instead) -- treat that exact pair as unverified; (b) neither abstract EXPLICITLY proves seed quality is prompt-specific rather than universal -- that is a sound inference from 2411.18810 tying reliability to composition/prompt plus the absence of any portability evidence, not a directly quoted result. The directional claim (mostly folklore, no portable magic number) holds.
- **Sources:** [Good Seed Makes a Good Crop: Discovering Secret Seeds in T2I Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14828) (Xu, Zhang et al., 2024) — Across 1024 seeds on SD2.0, golden seed FID 21.60 vs inferior 31.97; a classifier predicts the seed from the image with >99.9% accuracy, showing seeds leave distinct structural signatures. arXiv:2405.14828 ; [All Seeds Are Not Equal: Reliable Random Seeds for Compositional T2I](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18810) (Li et al., 2024) — Different seeds produce compositional accuracy from 41.0% down to 28.3% with statistical significance; reliability is tied to the prompt/composition, not a universal seed value. arXiv:2411.18810

### A weak/underspecified prompt produces a generic… · `recommended` · community-claim

**A weak/underspecified prompt produces a generic regression-to-the-mean image NO MATTER the seed -- this is the operator's exact failure mode.**

When the prompt under-constrains identity, the model fills the unconstrained degrees of freedom with the dataset average: a neutral, forgettable 'default person' in a default pose. Re-rolling the seed only re-samples WITHIN that generic basin -- you get a different generic nobody every time, never a striking character, because nothing in the conditioning pushes toward specificity. Community guidance is blunt: 'a castle' yields a generic fortress; adding specific descriptors slashes output randomness dramatically because the prompt now constrains the manifold.  [grounding: strong-community]

- **For the pipeline:** If 2-3 seed re-rolls all give different-but-equally-generic results, STOP re-rolling -- it is a prompt miss. The signature of a prompt miss is 'varied yet uniformly bland.' Add load-bearing identity tokens: distinct silhouette, specific clothing/material, age, explicit pose verb ('standing tall, weight forward'), and an emotional/character descriptor. Then re-roll. Do NOT touch tonemaps/lighting/render settings to fix a content problem.
- **Engine:** all · **Base:** all · **Kind:** technique
- **Verify:** CONFIRMED: Both community sources confirm the core claim. bulkimagegeneration.com states 'vague prompts are a fast track to generic or unpredictable results' (the cited '>60% randomness reduction' figure is confirmed verbatim from the source, though it is a vendor statistic with no published methodology -- do not treat the exact percentage as load-bearing). Prodia confirms under-specified prompts yield misaligned/generic output and specificity is required. The diagnostic signature -- 'varied yet uniformly bland' across re-rolls means prompt miss, not seed miss -- is sound and is the single most useful operational rule in this lane. The instruction to NOT touch tonemaps/lighting/render settings to fix a content problem is correct: those are orthogonal axes.
- **Sources:** [Stable Diffusion Prompt Guide for Better AI Art](https://bulkimagegeneration.com/blog/en/trends/stable-diffusion-prompt-guide) (bulkimagegeneration.com, 2024) — Vague prompts are a fast track to generic results; 'a castle' yields a generic fortress, while adding specific descriptors ('blue sky, wide-angle') reduces output randomness by over 60%. ; [10 Bad Prompt Mistakes in Stable Diffusion to Avoid](https://blog.prodia.com/post/10-bad-prompt-mistakes-in-stable-diffusion-to-avoid-now) (Prodia, 2024) — Under-specified prompts yield generic/unpredictable output; specificity (subject, posture, clothing, lighting) is required to align visuals with intent.
